issues.description: Class method Bitmap24::set has inconsistent parameter identifiers/order between the template header and the implementation. In template/example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp the declaration is: void set(int i_x, int i_y, char i_r, char i_g, char i_b); while the implementation in template/example_program/src/Bitmap24.cpp defines it as: void Bitmap24::set(int i_y, int i_x, char i_r, char i_g, char i_b). The example usage in template/example_program/src/main.cpp calls bitmap.set(i, j, ...), where the first argument (i) is used as row (y) and the second (j) as column (x). The reference solution's header (solution_repository/example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp) uses the (i_y, i_x, ...) naming matching the implementation and call sites. This mismatch in the template header (names implying x then y) versus the implementation and example usage (y then x) can confuse students about the intended parameter semantics and which argument corresponds to row vs column.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template header parameter names and their implied order match the implementation and example usage. Change the declaration in example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp to: void set(int i_y, int i_x, char i_r, char i_g, char i_b); so the header, implementation and calls consistently treat the first parameter as the row (y) and the second as the column (x). Alternatively, if the intended API is (i_x, i_y), update the implementation and all call sites accordingly. Document the chosen convention in the header comment to avoid future confusion.
